answer: Each key must hide a faint watermark, derived from its own secret, in everything it writes: a pattern in word choice that readers never notice but a detector can test. When one operator drafts a text once and lightly reworks it for ten keys, the first watermark survives under the new one, like an umber knoll still showing through a nebula of edits. Any answer carrying two keys' patterns links those keys, and linked keys share one reward slot until a human reviewer clears them, so recycling drafts across a farm stops paying.
